title: Me dijo que vendría: reported speech
summary: Pass on what people said, asked and asked you to do: tenses step back, questions take si or keep their question word, and here and now become there and then.
focus: Reported speech: backshift of tenses, reported questions and requests, and shifting time and place words
content:
## Reporting what someone said

To pass on someone's words you need a reporting verb and **que**: **decir** (to say, tell), **contar** (to tell, recount), **explicar** (to explain), **comentar** (to mention), **añadir** (to add), **prometer** (to promise). Questions take **preguntar**; requests take **pedir**.

If the reporting verb is in the present, nothing shifts:

- «Estoy cansada.» → **Dice que está cansada.** (She says she's tired.)

If it is in the past (**dijo, contó, explicó…**), the reported verb usually steps one place back in time. This is the *backshift*:

- «Estoy cansada.» → **Dijo que estaba cansada.** (She said she was tired.)

## The backshift table

| Direct speech | Reported after **dijo que…** |
|---|---|
| present: «**Voy** al médico.» | imperfect: **iba** al médico |
| preterite: «**Fui** al médico.» | pluperfect: **había ido** (**fue** is also heard in speech) |
| present perfect: «**He ido**.» | pluperfect: **había ido** |
| future: «**Iré**.» | conditional: **iría** |
| imperfect / conditional: «**Iba**.» «**Iría**.» | no change: **iba**, **iría** |
| imperative: «**Ven**.» | **que** + imperfect subjunctive: **que viniera** |

**Still true?** Then you may keep the present: **Me dijo que es de Sevilla** (she still is). **Era** is just as correct; it tells the story from the past.

## Questions and requests

- Yes/no questions are reported with **si** (*whether*, no accent): «¿Tienes coche?» → **Me preguntó si tenía coche.**
- Questions with a question word keep it, accent and all: «¿Dónde vives?» → **Me preguntó dónde vivía.** «¿Qué quieres?» → **Me preguntó qué quería.**
- Orders and requests become **pedir que** or **decir que** + subjunctive; after a past verb, the imperfect subjunctive:
  - «Llámame.» → **Me pidió que la llamara.** (She asked me to call her.)
  - «No toquéis nada.» → **Nos dijo que no tocáramos nada.** (He told us not to touch anything.)

**Decir que** + indicative passes on information; **decir que** + subjunctive passes on an order.

## Here becomes there: time and place words

Words that point at the speaker's *here and now* shift when you report them somewhere else or later:

| Direct | Reported |
|---|---|
| **aquí** | **allí** |
| **hoy** | **aquel día** |
| **ayer** | **el día anterior** |
| **mañana** | **al día siguiente** |
| **ahora** | **entonces** |
| **este / esta** | **ese / esa** (or **aquel / aquella**) |

- «Volveré aquí mañana.» → **Dijo que volvería allí al día siguiente.** (He said he would come back there the next day.)

Persons shift too: «**mi** hermano» → **su hermano**.

vocabulary.example: Mi abuela nos contó que de joven había vivido en Cuba.
vocabulary.example_meaning: My grandmother told us that she had lived in Cuba as a young woman.

vocabulary.example: El camarero nos preguntó si queríamos postre.
vocabulary.example_meaning: The waiter asked us whether we wanted dessert.

vocabulary.example: El jefe me pidió que revisara el informe.
vocabulary.example_meaning: The boss asked me to check the report.

vocabulary.example: La guía nos explicó que el museo cerraba los lunes.
vocabulary.example_meaning: The guide explained to us that the museum closed on Mondays.

vocabulary.example: Pablo comentó que el piso nuevo era muy luminoso.
vocabulary.example_meaning: Pablo mentioned that the new flat was very bright.

vocabulary.example: Luego añadió que no hacía falta reservar.
vocabulary.example_meaning: Then he added that there was no need to book.

vocabulary.example: Me prometió que me devolvería el libro.
vocabulary.example_meaning: She promised me she would give the book back.

vocabulary.meaning: to let someone know, to warn
vocabulary.example: Nos avisó de que el tren saldría con retraso.
vocabulary.example_meaning: He let us know that the train would leave late.

vocabulary.meaning: the next day, the following day
vocabulary.example: Dijeron que vendrían al día siguiente.
vocabulary.example_meaning: They said they would come the next day.

vocabulary.meaning: the day before, the previous day
vocabulary.example: Me contó que había llegado el día anterior.
vocabulary.example_meaning: She told me she had arrived the day before.

vocabulary.example: Explicó que aquel día no tenía tiempo.
vocabulary.example_meaning: He explained that he didn't have time that day.

vocabulary.example: Te dejo un recado: dice Carmen que la llames.
vocabulary.example_meaning: Here's a message for you: Carmen says to call her.

quiz.prompt: Last Friday Ana said: «Hoy estoy agotada.» → Ana me dijo que aquel día ___ agotada.
quiz.explanation: After a past reporting verb the present steps back to the imperfect, and hoy becomes aquel día: 'Ana me dijo que aquel día estaba agotada.'
hints: Present in direct speech becomes the imperfect after dijo.

quiz.prompt: Luis: «Iré a la reunión.» → Luis me prometió que ___ a la reunión. (ir)
quiz.explanation: The future in direct speech becomes the conditional after a past reporting verb: iré → iría.
hints: Ir in the conditional, él form.

quiz.prompt: Marta: «Perdí las llaves ayer.» → Marta me contó que ___ las llaves el día anterior.
quiz.explanation: In careful reported speech a preterite becomes the pluperfect (había + participle): perdí → había perdido. In everyday speech the preterite (perdió, as at B1) is also heard. Ayer becomes el día anterior.
hints: The past before the past is the pluperfect.

quiz.prompt: Mi madre: «Ven a las ocho.» → Mi madre me pidió que ___ a las ocho. (venir)
quiz.explanation: A reported order takes que + subjunctive; after the past pidió it is the imperfect subjunctive: vinieron → viniera.
hints: An order after a past verb takes the imperfect subjunctive.

quiz.explanation: A yes/no question is reported with si (whether), without an accent: 'Me preguntó si tenía coche.'
hints: A yes/no question is introduced by whether.

quiz.prompt: «¿Dónde vives?» → Me preguntó ___ vivía. (keep the question word)
quiz.explanation: A question with a question word keeps it, accent included: 'Me preguntó dónde vivía.'
hints: The question word stays, with its accent.

quiz.prompt: Last week Pedro said: «Volveré mañana.» → Pedro dijo que volvería ___.
quiz.explanation: Reported a week later, mañana no longer means tomorrow: it becomes al día siguiente.
hints: Mañana from the speaker's point of view becomes the next day.

quiz.prompt: The teacher said: «El agua hierve a cien grados.» → La profesora nos explicó que el agua ___ a cien grados. (a fact that is still true)
quiz.explanation: A fact that is still true can keep the present after a past reporting verb: 'nos explicó que el agua hierve a cien grados'. Hervía would also be correct, but not the conditional or the pluperfect.

quiz.prompt: Rocío, about her village: «Aquí se come muy bien.» → Rocío comentó que ___ se comía muy bien. (aquí → ?)
quiz.explanation: Reported from somewhere else, aquí becomes allí: 'Rocío comentó que allí se comía muy bien.'

conversations.title: The landlord's call
conversations.scenario: Elena tells her flatmate Javier what their landlord said on the phone.

lines.speaker: b
lines.text: El casero. Me dijo que pasaría el jueves a revisar la caldera.
lines.meaning: The landlord. He said he would come by on Thursday to check the boiler.

lines.speaker: a
lines.text: ¿El jueves? ¿Le explicaste que trabajamos los dos?
lines.meaning: Thursday? Did you explain to him that we both work?

lines.speaker: b
lines.text: Sí, y me preguntó si alguno de nosotros podía quedarse en casa.
lines.meaning: Yes, and he asked me whether one of us could stay at home.

lines.speaker: b
lines.text: Le dije que lo hablaría contigo. También me pidió que le enviáramos una foto de la caldera.
lines.meaning: I told him I'd talk it over with you. He also asked us to send him a photo of the boiler.
lines.note: A request takes que + imperfect subjunctive

lines.speaker: a
lines.meaning: OK. Did he mention anything about the rent?

lines.speaker: b
lines.text: Sí, añadió que el año que viene lo subiría un poco.
lines.meaning: Yes, he added that next year he would put it up a little.

lines.speaker: a
lines.meaning: What a surprise! And did he tell you how much?

lines.speaker: b
lines.text: No. Me prometió que nos lo explicaría todo el jueves.
lines.meaning: No. He promised he would explain it all to us on Thursday.

listening.text: Mi hermano dijo que tenía hambre.
listening.meaning: My brother said he was hungry.

listening.text: Nos preguntaron si queríamos más café.
listening.meaning: They asked us whether we wanted more coffee.

listening.text: El médico me explicó que no era nada grave.
listening.meaning: The doctor explained to me that it was nothing serious.

listening.text: Mi vecina me pidió que le regara las plantas.
listening.meaning: My neighbour asked me to water her plants.

listening.text: Me contó que había vivido tres años en Lisboa.
listening.meaning: She told me she had lived in Lisbon for three years.

listening.text: La abogada añadió que al día siguiente firmarían el contrato.
listening.meaning: The lawyer added that they would sign the contract the next day.
listening.note: New word: la abogada = the lawyer.

listening.text: El conductor nos avisó de que el autobús no pararía en aquella calle.
listening.meaning: The driver warned us that the bus would not stop in that street.

guide.tip: Ask when the words were said. If the reporting verb is in the past, step each verb one place back unless the fact is still true.

bites.title: Past verb, step back
bites.rule: After dijo, contó or explicó, the reported verb steps back: the present becomes the imperfect, the future becomes the conditional, and the preterite or perfect becomes the pluperfect.
bites.example: «Voy al cine.» → Dijo que iba al cine.
bites.example_meaning: 'I'm going to the cinema.' → He said he was going to the cinema.

bites.title: Orders become subjunctive
bites.rule: A reported order or request takes que + subjunctive; after a past verb, the imperfect subjunctive: ven becomes me pidió que viniera.
bites.example_meaning: She asked me to wait for her.

bites.title: Si or the question word
bites.rule: Yes/no questions are reported with si (no accent); other questions keep their question word with its accent: qué, dónde, cuándo.
bites.example: Me preguntó si tenía hambre y qué quería comer.
bites.example_meaning: He asked me whether I was hungry and what I wanted to eat.

bites.title: Here and now move
bites.rule: Hoy becomes aquel día, mañana becomes al día siguiente, ayer becomes el día anterior, aquí becomes allí and este becomes ese. A fact that is still true needs no backshift.
bites.example: Dijo que volvería allí al día siguiente.
bites.example_meaning: He said he would come back there the next day.

sorts.title: Which tense after dijo que?
sorts.why: The present becomes the imperfect, the preterite or perfect becomes the pluperfect, the future becomes the conditional, and the imperative becomes que + imperfect subjunctive.

sorts.title: Si or the question word?
sorts.why: Yes/no questions are reported with si; questions with qué, dónde, cuándo… keep that word.

spots.sentence: Ana dijo que vendrá al día siguiente.
spots.why: After a past reporting verb, the future becomes the conditional.

spots.sentence: Me preguntó sí quería un café.
spots.why: Reported yes/no questions use si (whether), no accent.

spots.sentence: Me pidió que la llamaba por la tarde.
spots.why: A reported request takes the imperfect subjunctive after pidió.

spots.sentence: Nos contó que aquel día ha perdido el tren.
spots.why: A perfect in direct speech becomes the pluperfect when reported in the past.
The question word keeps its accent in a reported question.

builds.text: Me dijo que estaba muy ocupada.
builds.meaning: She told me she was very busy.
We asked him whether he wanted to come.

builds.text: Nos pidió que habláramos más bajo.
builds.meaning: She asked us to speak more quietly.

builds.text: Prometió que lo haría al día siguiente.
builds.meaning: He promised he would do it the next day.
